baslik: Does Apple Cider Vinegar Lower Blood Sugar?
yorum: Have you ever tried apple cider vinegar before a meal? Did you notice any difference, or did you stop because of the taste?
aciklama_giris:
In a small trial of 12 healthy young adults, a drink of liquid vinegar before a starchy meal made the blood sugar rise in the first hour about 31 percent smaller than water did. Pooled reviews agree that vinegar can modestly lower the after-meal rise, but the trials are small and short, and reviewers rate the certainty of the evidence as very low.

In this video we look at what the studies actually found, how acetic acid may slow the stomach, why the evidence is thinner than the headlines, and the safety points about teeth, the throat, tablets and medication. We finish with practical, careful ways to use vinegar, if you choose to.

sahneler.metin: If you take apple cider vinegar before meals to calm your blood sugar, here is what one small trial found.
sahneler.gorsel: a tall glass bottle of apple cider vinegar with a cork stopper on a kitchen table, a small glass of golden apple cider vinegar beside it, two whole apples, morning light

sahneler.metin: At Arizona State University, twelve healthy adults ate the same starchy meal on different days. When they drank liquid vinegar first, their blood sugar rise in the first hour was about 31 percent smaller than with water.
sahneler.gorsel: a glass of apple cider vinegar beside a plate of white pasta and a bread roll, a glucose meter with a blank screen, a gentle rolling hill line drawn above the plate

baslik.not: smaller rise in the first hour, 12 adults

sahneler.metin: By the end, you'll know how big the effect really is, why the evidence is thinner than the headlines, and how to try vinegar safely if you want to.
sahneler.gorsel: an open notebook with blank pages, a pair of round eyeglasses, a small glass bottle of apple cider vinegar and a single apple on a wooden desk

sahneler.metin: So does apple cider vinegar really lower blood sugar? Today we'll look at the studies, the way it may work in your stomach, and the safety points that rarely make it onto the label.
sahneler.gorsel: a large magnifying glass held over a bottle of apple cider vinegar and a halved apple, small hexagon ring molecule sketches around them joined by dashed callout lines

sahneler.metin: Welcome to The Food Almanac. Let's begin with what a blood sugar spike is, and why people try to soften it.

kart.alt: What it does to your blood sugar

sahneler.metin: When you eat bread, rice, pasta or potatoes, your digestive system breaks the starch down into glucose, a simple sugar that passes into your bloodstream.
sahneler.gorsel: a slice of bread, a bowl of white rice, some pasta and a potato, small golden glucose spheres rising from them, simple hexagon ring chains breaking apart

sahneler.metin: Your pancreas answers by releasing insulin, a hormone that helps move that glucose into your muscles and other tissues. Blood sugar rises, and then settles back down.
sahneler.gorsel: textbook engraving of the pancreas beside the small intestine, green insulin particles drifting into a tube-shaped vessel with small red discs, dashed lines to a muscle fiber

baslik.not: helps move glucose into your cells

sahneler.metin: In type 2 diabetes and prediabetes, this system works less smoothly. The same meal can push blood sugar higher, and keep it high for longer.
sahneler.gorsel: a tube-shaped vessel crowded with golden glucose spheres between small red discs, next to a muscle cell with small closed gates on its surface

sahneler.metin: That is why a cheap kitchen ingredient that might soften the rise gets so much attention. Vinegar has been tested for exactly this in small trials for years.
sahneler.gorsel: a kitchen shelf with a bottle of apple cider vinegar, a wooden spoon, a bowl of apples and a small glucose meter with a blank screen

sahneler.metin: Apple cider vinegar is mostly water and acetic acid, the compound that gives it that sharp smell. In one trial, a dose of 25 grams, a little under two tablespoons, supplied about 1.25 grams of acetic acid.
sahneler.gorsel: a glass measuring spoon filled with apple cider vinegar beside a bottle of apple cider vinegar, a simple two-carbon acetic acid molecule sketch with dashed callout lines

baslik.not: in a 25 gram dose of vinegar

sahneler.metin: Let's start with the kind of study that gets quoted most: a test meal, with and without vinegar.
Researchers led by Carol Johnston ran a crossover trial. Fifteen young adults signed up, twelve finished, with an average age of about 23 and no diabetes.
sahneler.gorsel: a quiet research room with a single chair at a table, a glucose meter with a blank screen, a glass of apple cider vinegar and a covered meal tray, tall window

sahneler.metin: Each person ate the same test meal, with 64 grams of carbohydrate, on four different days. Once with plain water, once with liquid vinegar, and twice with vinegar tablets.
sahneler.gorsel: four small glass cups in a row on a tray: plain water, apple cider vinegar, whole vinegar tablets, and crushed tablets dissolved in water, a plate of pasta and bread behind them

baslik.not: of carbohydrate in the test meal

sahneler.metin: In the first hour, the blood sugar rise was smallest after liquid vinegar, about 31 percent lower than with water. Whole vinegar tablets did no better than water.

grafik.baslik: Blood sugar rise in the first hour
grafik.alt: Area under the curve, mmol·h/L · lower is better
grafik.kaynak: Feise & Johnston, J Nutr Metab 2020 · 12 healthy adults, 64 g carbohydrate meal

sahneler.metin: It is a neat result, but look at the limits. Twelve young, healthy people, one meal, and blood sugar measured for only the first hour. The authors said so themselves.
sahneler.gorsel: a single plate of pasta and bread on a laboratory bench next to a glass of apple cider vinegar and a small stack of research papers with blank pages

sahneler.metin: Many similar small trials exist, including some in people with diabetes. So researchers began to pool them, to see whether the pattern holds up when you add everything together.
sahneler.gorsel: several small glass jars of golden apple cider vinegar being poured into one large glass beaker on a laboratory bench, an antique brass scale beside it

sahneler.metin: In 2017, Shishehbor and colleagues pooled controlled trials of vinegar taken with a meal. Blood sugar and insulin after eating were lower with vinegar than without it.
sahneler.gorsel: a glass of apple cider vinegar beside a plate of rice and bread, two gentle hill-shaped lines drawn above it, one tall and one lower, calm and minimal
sahneler.etiket: Shishehbor et al. · Diabetes Res Clin Pract · 2017

sahneler.metin: A larger review in 2022, from Imperial College London, searched for randomized trials of vinegar and related compounds. It covered 46 studies and 913 people in total, across all short-chain fatty acids, not vinegar alone.
sahneler.gorsel: a library table stacked with journals with blank covers, an oil lamp, a bottle of apple cider vinegar and a teacup with rising steam
sahneler.etiket: Cherta-Murillo et al. · Am J Clin Nutr · 2022

sahneler.metin: For vinegar taken once with a meal, the blood sugar response was lower in people with type 2 diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance. But that pooled result rested on just 67 people.
sahneler.gorsel: a small group of sixty-seven tiny round pebbles in a glass dish beside a glass of apple cider vinegar and a glucose meter with a blank screen

baslik.not: behind the pooled result in diabetes and prediabetes

sahneler.metin: In healthy volunteers, the effect was smaller still, sitting right at the edge of statistical significance. That fits with a simple idea: people with smaller spikes have less to gain.
sahneler.gorsel: an apple cider vinegar bottle and a halved apple on a table, beside them a low flat gentle wave line, calm and minimal

sahneler.metin: What about drinking it every day for weeks? A 2018 review looked at 11 studies in 278 people with diabetes. Pooling three trials of 147 people, the HbA1c, a three-month blood sugar marker, fell by about 0.4 percentage points after 8 to 12 weeks.
sahneler.gorsel: a laboratory bench with a rack of small capped sample tubes, a glass of apple cider vinegar and a wall calendar with blank pages
sahneler.etiket: Siddiqui et al. · J Evid Based Integr Med · 2018

sahneler.metin: Fasting blood sugar was also slightly lower, by about 0.8 millimoles per liter, which is roughly 14 milligrams per deciliter. A modest change, from only three small trials.
sahneler.gorsel: a spoon of apple cider vinegar over a glass of water in the early morning, a glucose meter with a blank screen on the table

sahneler.metin: That sounds promising. But the authors of that review wrote that the quantity and quality of evidence was insufficient to be sure about either effectiveness or safety.
sahneler.gorsel: a scholar's desk with an open notebook with blank pages, a bottle of apple cider vinegar and a hand-drawn question mark shape made of apple peel

sahneler.metin: So how might a splash of vinegar change what happens in your body? The leading idea involves your stomach.
Your stomach acts as a gatekeeper. It releases food into the small intestine a little at a time, a process called gastric emptying.
sahneler.gorsel: textbook engraving of the stomach with its lower valve, the pylorus, letting a small portion of food into the small intestine, clean educational plate

sahneler.metin: If that release slows down, starch reaches the intestine more gradually, and glucose enters your blood more slowly. A flatter curve, rather than a sharp peak.
sahneler.gorsel: a stomach holding apple cider vinegar and rice, releasing a thin slow stream of golden glucose spheres into the small intestine, next to a low gentle hill line

sahneler.metin: A 2007 pilot study tested this in ten people with type 1 diabetes and a slow stomach, called gastroparesis. They drank 30 milliliters of apple cider vinegar in water before breakfast for two weeks.
sahneler.gorsel: a tall glass of water with a small measure of apple cider vinegar beside a bowl of rice pudding and a spoon, a small stomach sketch in the corner

sahneler.metin: Using ultrasound after a rice pudding meal, the researchers found that stomach emptying fell from a median of 27 percent to 17 percent. So in these patients, vinegar did slow the stomach.
sahneler.gorsel: a stomach next to a bowl of rice pudding and a glass of apple cider vinegar, a slow trickle of food leaving the stomach, an antique pocket watch beside them

sahneler.metin: But notice the catch. These patients' stomachs already emptied too slowly. The authors warned that slowing them further could be a disadvantage for blood sugar control. We'll come back to this in the safety part.
sahneler.gorsel: a stomach sketched with a closed valve and a glass of apple cider vinegar beside it, a small caution flag made of cloth on a stick

baslik.not: for people whose stomach already empties slowly

sahneler.metin: One more thing matters here. In the tablet trial, whole vinegar tablets did no better than water. And a separate team tested eight tablet products and were unsure whether apple cider vinegar was even present in some of them.
sahneler.gorsel: a small glass dish of round vinegar tablets beside a bottle of apple cider vinegar, a small scale and a magnifying glass over the tablets
sahneler.etiket: Hill et al. · J Am Diet Assoc · 2005

sahneler.metin: Now for the honest part. Why is the evidence thinner than the headlines suggest?
Most of these trials are small, often with only a few dozen people or fewer. A lot of them test a single meal in a lab, not months of ordinary life.
sahneler.gorsel: a single bottle of apple cider vinegar and a plate of pasta on a laboratory bench, an empty chair, a stopwatch beside the plate

sahneler.metin: In the 2022 review, 47 percent of the studies had a high risk of bias, and the authors found signs of publication bias for several outcomes. That is when small studies with exciting results are more likely to get published.
sahneler.gorsel: a stack of research folders with blank covers, the top few folders glowing slightly, one apple cider vinegar bottle on the shelf behind them

sahneler.metin: Results for daily use varied enormously from trial to trial, and the reviewers rated the overall certainty of the evidence as very uncertain.
sahneler.gorsel: a row of glass jars of apple cider vinegar each filled to a very different height on a wooden shelf, an antique brass scale tilted at the end

sahneler.metin: Doses and products differed too. Apple cider vinegar, white vinegar, wine vinegar, even tablets. About 15 to 20 grams, roughly one to two tablespoons, was common.
sahneler.gorsel: a small shelf with a bottle of apple cider vinegar, a bottle of white vinegar, a bottle of wine vinegar and a dish of tablets, a wooden spoon in front

sahneler.metin: So what is false? Vinegar does not make carbohydrates disappear, or cancel out a large dessert. And nothing in this research shows it can replace diabetes treatment.
sahneler.gorsel: a large slice of layered cake on a plate next to a small glass of apple cider vinegar, the glass looking tiny beside the cake

sahneler.metin: A fair summary is this. A modest nudge to the rise after a starchy meal, seen mostly in small short trials. Interesting, but not a proven treatment.
sahneler.gorsel: an apple cider vinegar bottle on a table next to a plate of rice and vegetables, a low gentle hill line drawn above the plate, calm morning light

sahneler.metin: Before you reach for the bottle, a few safety points. This is where vinegar's acidity matters.
Start with teeth. In one laboratory study, 190 extracted human teeth were soaked in nine acidic liquids. Vinegar and apple cider caused some of the greatest mineral loss.
sahneler.gorsel: a row of extracted human teeth in small glass dishes beside a bottle of apple cider vinegar, a magnifying glass over one tooth
sahneler.etiket: Maladkar et al. · Eur J Dent · 2022

baslik.not: vinegar eroded the most in a lab test

sahneler.metin: That was teeth in a dish, without saliva, so it cannot tell us how much harm real drinking does. But it is a good reason to dilute vinegar, and not to sip it all day.
sahneler.gorsel: a tall glass of water with a splash of apple cider vinegar beside a toothbrush resting in a ceramic cup, soft window light

sahneler.metin: Then the throat. Undiluted vinegar can burn. A 2020 case report described a 15-year-old who drank a vinegar beverage every day without enough dilution, and developed ulcers along the esophagus. He recovered with treatment.
sahneler.gorsel: a bottle of apple cider vinegar with a small caution flag beside a glass of water, a textbook engraving of the throat and esophagus in an inset circle

sahneler.metin: Tablets carry their own risks. In 2005, after a report of esophageal injury linked to apple cider vinegar tablets, researchers found that tablet size, acidity and acid content varied widely between products.
sahneler.gorsel: a handful of round vinegar tablets in a glass dish beside a bottle of apple cider vinegar, a small caution flag, a magnifying glass over the tablets
sahneler.etiket: Hill et al. · J Am Diet Assoc · 2005

sahneler.metin: Now medication. Reference sources note that large amounts of vinegar may lower potassium, which matters for people who take water pills or insulin. They also flag a possible overlap with some diabetes medicines.
sahneler.gorsel: a consultation desk with a stethoscope, a closed notebook, a bottle of apple cider vinegar, a few capsules in a dish and a glucose meter with a blank screen

baslik.not: ask your doctor or pharmacist first

sahneler.metin: That overlap is mostly a theoretical precaution, not something shown in trials. But it is reason enough to talk to your doctor or pharmacist before making vinegar a daily habit if you use these medicines.
sahneler.gorsel: a doctor's desk with a glass of diluted apple cider vinegar, a notebook with blank pages and a pen, a pill organizer beside a glucose meter

sahneler.metin: And remember the gastroparesis study. If you have diabetes with a slow stomach, vinegar may slow it further, so ask first. That is the detail we flagged earlier, and it can matter.
sahneler.gorsel: a stomach sketch with a slow trickle leaving it, a bottle of apple cider vinegar and a small caution flag on a wooden table

baslik.not: ask your doctor before trying vinegar

sahneler.metin: So if you still want to try it, here are four careful ways to use vinegar.

kart.alt: If you choose to try vinegar

sahneler.metin: One. Dilute it. The trials mostly used about one to two tablespoons of apple cider vinegar mixed into a glass of water, not a shot straight from the bottle.
sahneler.gorsel: a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar being stirred into a tall glass of water, a bottle of apple cider vinegar beside it

sahneler.metin: Two. Pair it with a starchy meal. In the trials, vinegar was taken with or shortly before the food. We don't know whether it helps when taken hours earlier, or on its own.
sahneler.gorsel: a glass of diluted apple cider vinegar beside a plate of pasta and bread, an antique pocket watch resting between them

sahneler.metin: Three. Protect your teeth and throat. Drink it diluted, don't sip it slowly through the day, and rinse your mouth with plain water afterward.
sahneler.gorsel: a glass of diluted apple cider vinegar next to a second glass of plain water, a toothbrush in a cup, soft window light

sahneler.metin: Four. Skip the tablets. In the one trial that compared them with liquid vinegar, whole tablets did no better than water, and product quality varies.
sahneler.gorsel: a dish of round vinegar tablets pushed to the side of a table, a glass of diluted apple cider vinegar in front, a bottle of apple cider vinegar behind

sahneler.metin: And keep it in proportion. Vinegar cannot undo a large plate of refined carbohydrates. If you have diabetes, kidney disease or take regular medication, check with your doctor or pharmacist before making it a habit.
sahneler.gorsel: a modest dinner plate of grilled fish, roasted vegetables and a small portion of rice, a glass of diluted apple cider vinegar beside it

sahneler.metin: Let's recap.

kart.baslik: A small nudge, not a cure
kart.alt: What vinegar can and cannot do

sahneler.metin: In small trials, vinegar taken with a starchy meal lowered the rise in blood sugar afterward, by about 31 percent in one study of twelve young adults.
sahneler.gorsel: a glass of apple cider vinegar beside a plate of pasta and bread and a glucose meter with a blank screen, a low gentle hill line above the plate

sahneler.metin: Pooled reviews agree on a modest effect, bigger in people with diabetes or prediabetes. But the trials are small and short, and reviewers rate the certainty as very low.
sahneler.gorsel: a tidy stack of research folders with blank covers beside a bottle of apple cider vinegar and an antique brass scale, evenly balanced

sahneler.metin: It may work by slowing the stomach. That is also why it needs care with a slow stomach, with tablets, with undiluted drinking, and with some medicines.
sahneler.gorsel: a bottle of apple cider vinegar beside a stomach sketch and a glass of diluted vinegar, a small caution flag on the table

sahneler.metin: If you try it, dilute it, pair it with a starchy meal, skip the tablets, and let your doctor know. A small habit, with small, honest expectations.
sahneler.gorsel: a glass of diluted apple cider vinegar, a halved apple and a bottle of apple cider vinegar on a wooden kitchen table in morning light

sahneler.metin: If you found this useful, subscribe to The Food Almanac for more food science, explained calmly and honestly. This video is for education only, and it isn't medical advice. See you in the next one.
